findings.title: Check the dataset actually being queried
findings.body: This passes the endpoint’s original `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`. Dashboard widget splitting can call `_get_event_stats(discover, ...)` for an error-only query while the original dataset is a metrics dataset; the eligibility helper then rejects upsampling for that metrics dataset, so the split error count is returned unadjusted even when all projects are allowlisted. Pass the scoped dataset so eligibility matches the query being executed.

findings.title: Substring matching misidentifies error-focused queries
findings.body: Checking for `event.type:error` anywhere in the raw query does not establish that the query selects error events. For example, `!event.type:error` contains this substring but selects non-error events, so an allowlisted Discover query can replace `count()` with `sum(sample_weight)` for transactions and return incorrect counts. Conversely, error-only queries expressed as `!event.type:transaction` are not recognized, so their counts are not upsampled. Determine the effective event-type filter from parsed query conditions rather than a substring check.
